title: The Double Protocol
premise: Bram Nystrom, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—a diplomatic entity that exists on no registry—receives a debt notice for a favor he never performed, signed with his own dead father's cipher. Following the paper trail, he uncovers the Double Protocol: a contingency his father helped draft that allows the Office to erase its own agents, and which is about to be activated to bury a financial scandal before Frankfurt's markets open. Hunted by the colleagues who trained him and shadowed by the stranger who invoked the debt, Bram must decide whether to sell the Protocol's master key—the one secret worth killing for—to a hostile intelligence buyer or expose it publicly. In the end, Bram burns the key in front of both sides, accepts erasure himself, and walks out of the system alive but officially nonexistent, inheriting nothing but his own name.
about_author: Felix Quintana is the pen name of a former trade journalist who spent a decade covering cross-border finance out of Brussels and Zurich. He writes thrillers about institutions that prefer their crimes unwitnessed.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Bram Nystrom's POV. A courier delivers an envelope invoking a 1999 favor Bram never performed, demanding repayment 'with interest' within seventy-two hours. The signature uses his father's dead-man cipher. Emotional beat: unease—the past knocking on a door Bram bricked over.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the unmarked Meridian Office, Bram requests archive access on his father's file and is smoothly denied by his handler, Voss, whose courtesy feels rehearsed. That night his apartment is searched—professionally, almost politely. Beat: dread dressed as routine.

chapters.title: The Stranger
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV. The stranger, Ilse, a disgraced forensic accountant, reveals she found the favor ledger while auditing a shell company: Bram's father once saved her mother's life, and the debt was never discharged. She wants Bram's help reaching the Protocol files. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Double Protocol
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Ilse shows him the fragment she recovered: a standing order authorizing the Office to liquidate its own personnel and their records. Bram realizes his father didn't write it—he tried to kill it, and died for it. Beat: inheritance as indictment.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss reports Bram's inquiries upward; the Office quietly activates preliminary erasure protocols on Bram's accounts, aliases, and safehouses. We see the machinery of institutional self-protection begin to turn. Beat: cold, procedural menace.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram and Ilse retrieve his father's hidden cache from a Geneva locker—half a key, physical and cryptographic. They're ambushed; Bram kills a man he trained. Beat: the first irreversible line crossed.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Desperate for leverage, Ilse contacts Marcus Reval, an intelligence broker, offering the Protocol key before Frankfurt opens Monday. Reval's interest confirms the secret's price—and paints a target. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Ghost Audit
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Tracing the shell companies, Bram finds the scandal beneath the Protocol: billions moved through Meridian channels into private hands, laundered across decades. His father discovered it in 1999. Beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Voss Offers Tea
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss meets Bram openly, offering reinstatement and protection if he surrenders the cache. Beneath the warmth, a threat to Ilse. Bram stalls. Beat: loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: Half a Key
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The cache's half-key is useless alone; the other half sits in the Office vault, accessible only to someone already flagged for erasure. Bram understands the trap: his father designed it so only a condemned man could finish it. Beat: grim admiration.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Hiding in Rotterdam, Ilse calculates their odds and hates the answer. She confesses she nearly sold the fragment to Reval already. Trust fractures. Beat: betrayal narrowly averted, scar left behind.

chapters.title: The Erasure List
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram steals a look at the current activation list: his name, Ilse's, and eleven others—including two directors who know too much. The Protocol isn't just cover-up; it's cannibalization. Beat: horror at the machine eating its own.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: Reval's POV. Reval sets his auction: the key goes to the highest bidder at market open Monday, whether or not Bram delivers. He tips the Office anonymously, playing both ends. Beat: the noose tightening from three directions.

chapters.title: Into the Vault
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Using his own erasure status as credentials, Bram infiltrates the Meridian vault during a staff purge and takes the second half of the key—and the full transaction ledger. Beat: triumph laced with vertigo.

chapters.title: What Father Left
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Deciphering the completed key, they find not a weapon but a testimony: his father's full record of the laundering, keyed to publish automatically unless affirmatively suppressed. The choice crystallizes: sell it, suppress it, or let it speak. Beat: inheritance redefined as responsibility.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Ordered to finalize all erasures before Monday, Voss hesitates over one name—his own protégé years ago was on an old list, erased without ceremony. Doubt cracks his obedience. Beat: the corrupter corrupted by conscience.

chapters.title: Auction Night
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram walks into Reval's auction carrying the key, watched by Office shooters and bidders from three services. He lets them bid, memorizes every face, then announces the key is worthless: publication is already armed on a dead-man timer. Beat: controlled detonation.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, intercut. As Frankfurt opens, the testimony publishes worldwide. Reval's buyers scatter, the Office scrambles to contain what can't be contained, and Voss makes his choice—feeding Bram the extraction window instead of the kill order. Beat: chaos as catharsis.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram submits to formal erasure—records dissolved, identity struck—to slip the retaliation net. Watching his own life deleted entry by entry, he feels not loss but release. Beat: survival at the cost of existence.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse delivers the ledger evidence to prosecutors in three jurisdictions, paying her family's debt in full. She and Bram part at a train platform—no debts between them now. Beat: quiet, earned closure.

chapters.title: The Man Without a File
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Months later, Bram lives under his real name in a city where nobody checks papers, working ordinary work. A Meridian remnant sends feelers; he doesn't answer. Beat: peace purchased, vigilance kept.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, coda. Bram receives a plain envelope: inside, a receipt marked PAID IN FULL, in his father's cipher. Some debts are settled only by becoming worthy of them. He burns it, smiles, and closes the door. Beat: resolution—the inheritance finally accepted.
